definition.interpretation: The initial experiment produced inconclusive results; divergence rate was within variance (observed ~0.066, prediction >= 0.05), suggesting that noise in the dynamic gridworld may mask subtle path-dependent preferences or that the agent's memory capacity was not fully utilized in this specific training regime.
definition.limitations: The observed divergence rate is statistically close to the noise floor, failing to provide a clear distinction from standard Markovian agents.
definition.next_step: Introduce deterministic gridworld parameters and increase episode count to isolate path-dependent effects from stochastic environment noise.

definition.method: Execute a comparative RL training run between a standard DQN and a recurrent DQN agent in a 10x10 deterministic gridworld with fixed reward sparsity.
definition.stop: Completion of 5 measurement sets across 3 seeds.
definition.success: A statistically significant difference (p < 0.05) in policy divergence between recurrent and non-recurrent agents over 20,000 episodes.

definition.reason: Prior experiment was inconclusive due to high variance; moving to deterministic environment to isolate path dependence.
definition.uncertainty: It remains unclear if memory-augmented agents form stable preferences or merely store transient state history.
